high.title: State Bank of Vietnam: Isolated phenomenon of some banks adjusting interest rates upward
high.summary: The State Bank of Vietnam (SBV) issued a press release addressing interest rate stabilization amid reports of some banks raising rates. SBV emphasized it has proactively implemented monetary policy measures to control inflation, stabilize macroeconomics, and promote economic growth. The central bank continues maintaining current policy rates to provide low-cost funding access for credit institutions, supporting the economy. SBV issued Circular 2342 on March 30, 2026, requiring credit institutions to focus on stabilizing market interest rates. A meeting with commercial banks was held April 9, 2026, to unify implementation of government policies aimed at reducing market interest rates to support businesses and citizens. This statement is crucial for VND traders as it signals SBV's commitment to keeping rates low despite some banks' upward adjustments, potentially supporting economic growth but raising questions about monetary policy effectiveness amid global rate pressures.

high.title: SBV determined to "cool down" interest rates
high.summary: SBV faces multiple pressures in monetary policy management as global geopolitical tensions, particularly escalating Middle East conflicts, create significant pressure on international commodity and financial markets. Brent oil maintains an upward trend, raising inflation risks in major economies. Major central banks like Fed, ECB, and BOE maintain cautious policies, with some (Australia, Ireland, Philippines) raising rates in early 2026. The USD strengthened amid increased safe-haven demand, pressuring domestic exchange rates, interest rates, and money markets. SBV acknowledges elevated cost-push inflation risks from external factors including oil, food prices, and supply chain disruptions. This creates a challenging environment for VND/USD management and domestic rate policy, as SBV must balance supporting economic growth while managing external pressures that could destabilize the currency and push up domestic inflation.

medium.title: Gold bars fall to lowest level in over 4 months, what do experts advise?
medium.summary: Global gold dropped to $4,504/ounce amid stable US Treasury yields, stronger USD, and Fed's hawkish rhetoric on inflation. Domestic gold prices followed suit, with SJC gold bars trading at 159-162 million VND/tael, down 400,000 VND/tael both ways. This marks gold's lowest level since early January 2026, reflecting increased pressure from rising oil prices and inflation concerns that may delay Fed rate cuts.

medium.title: Gold ring, gold bar prices on May 24
medium.summary: Domestic gold maintained low levels with SJC bars at 158-161 million VND/tael buy-sell spread. Major dealers quoted similar levels at 158.5-161.5 million VND/tael. Gold rings traded at the same range with 3 million VND/tael spread maintained. Prices remain at lowest since early January 2026, having dropped 1.9-2.3 million VND/tael from last week.

medium.title: One bank sets target profit of 86,000 billion VND, aims for TOP 100 Asia by 2030
medium.summary: BIDV announced strategic plans for 2026-2030, targeting to become a leading GREEN - LARGE - STRONG Financial-Banking Group in Southeast Asia, aiming for TOP 100 strongest banks in Asia by 2030. BIDV targets CASA ratio of 25-30% by 2030, NIM of 2.5-2.7%, improved ROA and ROE, and CIR below 30%. Pre-tax profit target reaches 86,000 billion VND by 2030 with CAR around 10.7%.

medium.title: Expert forecasts a "super wave" of $50 billion may hit Vietnam stock market
medium.summary: ABS's Nguyen The Minh noted Vietnam stock market growth outlook downgraded from "positive" to "neutral" after VN-Index fell 2.3% last week. Asian markets continue leading growth with Korea's Kospi and Taiwan's TAIEX upgraded to "rising" trend. Global bond yields cooled after early week surge on US-Iran deal expectations, with USD and VIX slowing their pace of increase.

medium.title: 100,000 billion VND blockbuster stirs IPO activity, Vietnam securities market set for new listings series
medium.summary: DMX (Dien May Xanh Investment) received approval for IPO of 180 million shares at 80,000 VND/share, raising 14,360 billion VND - the largest IPO in years. Post-IPO valuation reaches over 102,460 billion VND, potentially qualifying for VN30 inclusion after August listing. Other upcoming IPOs include LPBS (4,300 billion VND expected) and several entertainment companies.
